title: Haryana, Chandigarh, Tripura, Mizoram, Chhattisgarh and the Andaman Islands — filling the gaps
selection: These six states and UTs had only 3–7 places each. This pack adds their next most-visited places (Gurugram and Surajkund; Chandigarh's museum, plaza, zoo and sanctuary; Kamalasagar; Hmuifang, Tamdil and Lunglei; Bilaspur and Bastar's temples; South Andaman's beaches and Barren Island), researched from Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism).

HR1.claim: Haryana runs from the Shivalik Hills in the north-east to the Aravallis in the south.

evidence.quote: from the Shivalik Hills in the northeast to the Aravalli Range in the south

HR2.claim: Haryana was the setting of the battles of Panipat and the Kurukshetra war.

evidence.quote: having been the battleground for famous conflicts like the battles at Panipat and the legendary Kurukshetra war

GGN1.claim: Gurugram grew from a farming town into 'Cyber City', a business hub; Cyber Hub is its food and entertainment centre.

evidence.quote: From its humble origins as a sleepy agricultural town to its current status as a thriving business hub
earning it the moniker "Cyber City."
a food and entertainment destination that offers a tantalizing array of dining options

GGN2.claim: Sultanpur National Park near Gurugram is home to over 250 bird species.

evidence.quote: a bird sanctuary that is home to over 250 species of birds

BAO1.claim: This 18th-century stepwell at Farrukhnagar was built of stone, lime and brick; its shaft goes down more than 100 ft.

evidence.quote: Constructed back in the 18th century AD by Mughal emperor Ghaus Khan
Built out of stone, lime plaster and bricks
The shaft of the well was sunk to a depth of more than a hundred feet

HTM1.claim: The Heritage Transport Museum shows India's transport history: carriages, steam locomotives, vintage cars and the Ambassador.

evidence.quote: the museum is a living embodiment of Indian transport history
the iconic Ambassador car marked the beginning of a new era in the field of Indian transportation

SRJ1.claim: Surajkund, near Faridabad, is a reservoir believed to date to the 10th century and hosts the annual Surajkund Mela, one of India's largest craft fairs.

evidence.quote: Surajkund Lake, an ancient reservoir believed to date back to the 10th century
making it one of the largest handloom and handicraft fairs in India

SRJ2.claim: Faridabad's 18th-century Raja Nahar Singh Palace recalls the Jat rulers.

evidence.quote: The Raja Nahar Singh Palace, a beautiful 18th-century structure, gives you a glimpse into the life of the Jat rulers.

CH1.claim: Chandigarh was planned by Le Corbusier on a grid, below the Shivalik hills.

evidence.quote: Envisioned by the renowned Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier, Chandigarh offers a unique grid-like design
A city with the breathtaking backdrop of the Shivalik mountain range

CH_AIR.claim: Chandigarh's airport is Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport (IXC).

evidence.quote: Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport (IXC)

CH_BIRDS.claim: In winter, Sukhna Lake draws migratory birds such as Siberian ducks, storks and cranes.

evidence.quote: Sukhna Lake transforms into a haven for birdwatchers during the winter months when you can catch a glimpse of exotic migratory birds like Siberian ducks, storks, and cranes!

GMC1.claim: The Government Museum and Art Gallery holds collections moved from Lahore's Central Museum after Partition, in a Le Corbusier building.

evidence.quote: Formerly housed in Lahore's Central Museum, these precious treasures found sanctuary in Chandigarh's embrace
A testament to Le Corbusier's visionary genius, the building boasts a bold use of exposed reinforced concrete

S17_1.claim: Sector 17 Plaza, designed by Le Corbusier, is Chandigarh's shopping and gathering heart; the Capitol Complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evidence.quote: But Le Corbusier envisioned Sector 17 as more than just a shopping destination.
With tree-lined walkways, fountains, and open spaces
Chandigarh Capitol Complex: A UNESCO World Heritage Site

ZOO1.claim: Chhatbir Zoo (Mahendra Chaudhary Zoological Park), opened in 1977, covers 202 acres and is north-west India's largest zoo.

evidence.quote: Established in 1977 as part of the Chhatbir protected forest area, this magnificent zoo is officially known as the Mahendra Chaudhary Zoological Park.
Spanning an impressive 202 acres of raw scrubland, it stands as the largest zoological park in north-western India

SWS1.claim: Sukhna Wildlife Sanctuary has leopards, jungle cats, sambar and chital; guided treks run every month except June and September.

evidence.quote: such as the leopard and the jungle cat, while the sambhar and the chital roam freely
the sanctuary opens its gates every month, except September and June, inviting nature enthusiasts for guided treks

TR1.claim: Tripura has 19 tribal communities; the Unakoti rock carvings date to the 7th century.

evidence.quote: Among the 19 distinct tribal communities in Tripura
The ancient Unakoti rock carvings, dating back to the 7th century

TR2.claim: Fish curries — especially boiled hilsa with mustard seeds and green chillies — are central to Tripura's food.

evidence.quote: Fish curries, especially the famous boiled 'Hilsa' seasoned with mustard seeds and green chilies, take the spotlight.

KMS1.claim: Kamalasagar is a 10-acre lake dug in the 15th century, with the 16th-century Kasba Kali Bari temple on its shore.

evidence.quote: Kamalasagar Lake stretches 10 acres and is a sight to behold.
It is believed to have been excavated during the reign of Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the 15th century.
The lake's shores are home to the renowned Kamalasagar Kali Temple, also known as Kasba Kali Bari

HPA1.claim: Agartala's 12-acre Heritage Park showcases Tripura's culture and nature.

evidence.quote: Spread across 12 acres is a haven that seamlessly blends the rich cultural tapestry of Tripura with the pristine beauty of nature.

GMM1.claim: Gedu Mian Masjid, built in the 17th century, is one of Tripura's oldest and largest mosques.

evidence.quote: Gedu Mian Masjid was built during the 17th century, making it one of Tripura's oldest and largest mosques

DTE1.claim: Durgabari Tea Estate dates from the late 19th century and produces black tea.

evidence.quote: The Durgabari Tea Estate's inception dates back to the late 19th century during the British colonial era
ensures the production of high-quality black tea

HMF1.claim: Hmuifang, 50 km south of Aizawl, rises to 1,619 m; rhododendrons and orchids bloom here, and camping is popular.

evidence.quote: Located 50 kilometres south of Aizawl in Mizoram, Hmuifang Mountain stands at an elevation of 1,619 metres above sea level.
marked by the vibrant colours of rhododendrons and orchids during blooming seasons
Camping is another favoured activity

TAM1.claim: Tamdil, about 85 km from Aizawl, is Mizoram's largest natural lake; its name means 'Lake of Mustard'.

evidence.quote: Situated about 85 kilometres from Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram, Tamdil is a picturesque lake
The lake, whose name translates to 'Lake of Mustard' in Mizo
It is the largest natural lake in Mizoram

PLK1.claim: Palak Dil, near Phura village in the far south, is Mizoram's largest lake and good for birdwatching.

evidence.quote: Palak Dil or Pala Dipo is Mizoram’s largest lake, located near the Phura village which falls under the Saiha district
With its multiple avian species, Palak Lake is a gem for bird watchers.

SOL1.claim: Solomon's Temple, 10 km from Aizawl, is Mizoram's largest church; its foundation stone was laid in 1996.

evidence.quote: Behold Solomon's Temple, the largest church in Mizoram, located in the Kidron Valley, just 10 kilometres from Aizawl.
in 1996, amidst trials and triumphs, the vision came to life with the laying of the foundation stone

LUN1.claim: Lunglei — 'rock bridge' — is Mizoram's second-largest city, ringed by pine-meadow villages.

evidence.quote: The name 'Lunglei' literally means a rock bridge.
Charming villages nestled among pine meadows dot the untouched stretch of beautiful countryside surrounding Lunglei, the second-largest city in Mizoram.

BSP1.claim: Bilaspur is the base for Ratanpur's Mahamaya Temple, the Kalachuri temples of Malhar and Achanakmar Wildlife Sanctuary.

evidence.quote: From the revered Mahamaya Devi temple to the sprawling landscapes of the Achanakmar Wildlife Sanctuary
the powerful Kalachuri dynasty dominated the region, leaving behind iconic structures such as the Malhar temples

MMT1.claim: Ratanpur's Mahamaya Temple, to Durga and Mahalakshmi, dates from the 12th–13th centuries under the Kalachuris.

evidence.quote: Welcome to the revered Mahamaya Devi Temple, dedicated to Goddess Durga and Mahalakshmi, situated in the historic town of Ratanpur
Dating back to the 12th and 13th centuries, the Mahamaya Temple stands as a symbol of devotion, built under the patronage of the Kalachuri dynasty

BPL1.claim: Bastar Palace in Jagdalpur was the residence of Bastar's royal family, with a central dome and arched entrance.

evidence.quote: It was built by the rulers of Bastar
It served as the primary residence of the royal family and a centre for administrative activities.

DAN1.claim: The 600-year-old Danteshwari Temple at Dantewada is a Shakti Peetha, built by Kakatiya rulers in the 14th century.

evidence.quote: there is a 600-year old temple known as Danteshwari Temple
This temple dates back to the 14th century, built by the rulers of the Kakatiya dynasty

CHT1.claim: Chidiya Tapu, at the southern tip of South Andaman 28 km from Sri Vijaya Puram, is a birding spot with a horseshoe beach.

evidence.quote: Nestled on the southernmost tip of South Andaman Island, around 28 kilometres from Sri Vijaya Puram
Imagine a horseshoe-shaped beach

COR1.claim: Corbyn's Cove, a few km south of Sri Vijaya Puram, is a clean, family-friendly beach known for sunsets.

evidence.quote: located just a few kilometres south of Sri Vijaya Puram
Corbyn’s Cove Beach is also celebrated for its spectacular sunsets
which make it a family-friendly destination

WAN1.claim: Wandoor Beach, 25 km south-west of Sri Vijaya Puram, has a jetty for Jolly Buoy, Red Skin and Alexandra islands and glass-bottom boat trips.

evidence.quote: the Beach is easily accessible at just 25kms southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram
Its convenient jetty provides access to Jolly Buoy Island, Red Skin Island, and Alexandra Island
the area offers glass-bottom boat trips to nearby islands

MMN1.claim: Mount Manipur National Park, formerly Mount Harriet, is named for Manipur's role in the 1891 war; its peak is the islands' third highest at 1,257 ft.

evidence.quote: Mount Manipur, the crown jewel of the park, is the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago’s third tallest peak, soaring to a majestic 1,257 feet.
Renamed from Mount Harriet National Park to Manipur National Park in the honour of the cultural heritage of Manipur

BAR1.claim: Barren Island, 138 km north-east of Sri Vijaya Puram, is South Asia's only active volcano (last eruption 2017); its reefs suit advanced divers.

evidence.quote: Barren Island is approximately 138 kilometres northeast of Sri Vijaya Puram
It is renowned for being South Asia's only active volcano, which last erupted in 2017.
making it a popular spot for advanced divers

DHN1.claim: The Dhani Nallah mangrove walkway near Rangat is India's longest boardwalk of its kind.

evidence.quote: stands as the longest boardwalk of its kind in India
Located approximately 20 kilometres from Rangat mainland, adjacent to the Andaman Trunk Road
